meta.title: Double-booked car deck on the 07:40
meta.lede: Eleven car spaces on the Gannet's 07:40 from Varre to Holm were sold twice. Every driver crossed that morning, eleven of them on a relief sailing. What happened, why, and six follow-ups to commit to by number.

parts.markdown:
On Wednesday 9 September, the Gannet's 07:40 to Holm had 53 cars booked for 42 spaces. Crew caught it at the ramp check at 06:12. Every driver crossed that morning: 42 on the 07:40, and the 11 who booked last on a relief sailing at 09:10.

Two drivers missed the start of their shifts on Holm, and the harbour office took 64 calls before 09:00.

parts.title: Cars booked on the 07:40 through the evening before, against 42 spaces

spec.label: Drivers moved
spec.text: 11, to a relief sailing at 09:10, each with a full refund and a free return.

spec.label: Longest wait
spec.text: 1 hour 30 minutes at the Varre ramp.

spec.label: Office calls
spec.text: 64 before 09:00, against 9 on a normal Wednesday.

spec.label: Bookings lost
spec.text: None. Every double sale traces to one office terminal.

events.title: The 07:40 sells its last car space
events.markdown: Online sales reach 42 of 42 cars, and the app shows the deck as full.

events.title: The harbour office terminal reconnects
events.markdown: After a restart for an update, the terminal replays eleven car holds it had kept offline since the afternoon. The booking service accepts all eleven.

events.title: Crew count 53 cars booked for 42 spaces
events.markdown: The ramp check at Varre compares the loading list with the deck plan, and it does not add up.

events.title: Incident declared at SEV-2
events.markdown: Joss is paged and joins from home. Ines takes the office phones.

events.title: A relief sailing is agreed for 09:10
events.markdown: The Gannet's master agrees a second crossing, and the office texts the eleven drivers who booked last.

events.title: Every moved driver refunded
events.markdown: Eleven refunds and free returns go out, and offline holds are switched off on the terminal.

events.title: The relief sailing leaves with all eleven cars

items.title: Offline holds were replayed without a capacity check
items.summary: The terminal's replay path writes holds straight to the bookings table, past the check every other sale goes through.

facets.label: Evidence
facets.markdown: The booking log has eleven `hold.replay` events between 20:31:07 and 20:31:09, and none of them has a `capacity.check` span.

items.title: Nothing alerts when a sailing sells past capacity
items.summary: The oversale was in the data from 20:31, and nobody saw it for ten hours.

facets.label: Evidence
facets.markdown: The capacity dashboard showed 53 of 42 all night. Its alerts only cover payment failures.

items.title: Offline holds never expire
items.summary: The terminal had held those eleven places since 14:05, and would have replayed them days later.

items.title: Alert when any sailing sells past capacity
items.summary: A check every minute pages whoever is on call when bookings exceed spaces on any sailing.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: Nothing alerts when a sailing sells past capacity, and ten hours passed between the double sale and the ramp check.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: A query compares bookings with deck spaces for every sailing in the next 72 hours, once a minute, and pages on any excess.

facets.label: Done when
facets.markdown: Replaying the 9 September data in staging pages within two minutes.

items.title: Show cars sold against spaces on the loading list
items.summary: The crew's loading list opens with cars sold against spaces, in ochre when they do not fit.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: Crew found the problem at 06:12 by counting the list against the deck plan.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: The list header shows the count, such as 53 of 42, and marks each car sold after the deck was full.

facets.label: Note
facets.markdown: Shipped on 11 September in crew app 2.8.1.

items.title: A runbook for an overbooked sailing
items.summary: One page on who to call, how to arrange a relief sailing, and what to offer the drivers moved.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: The 28 minutes from 06:20 to 06:48, spent finding out who could approve a relief sailing.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: A page in the office handbook with the masters' numbers, the relief sailing checklist, and the standard offer of a refund and a free return.

items.title: Tell the last drivers before they set off
items.summary: When a sailing is oversold, the drivers who booked last get a message and a held place on the next sailing.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: Eleven drivers learned at the ramp, some after a long drive to Varre.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: The oversale alert messages each driver past capacity, in booking order, with a held place on the next sailing and a free cancellation.

facets.label: Done when
facets.markdown: In staging, an oversold sailing sends every message within five minutes of the alert.

items.title: Check capacity when the terminal replays holds
items.summary: Replayed holds go through the same capacity check as every other sale, and fail in plain sight when a deck is full.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: Offline holds were replayed without a capacity check.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: The replay path calls `booking.Hold` instead of inserting rows, and the terminal lists each refused hold with the next sailing that has room.

facets.label: Done when
facets.markdown: A replay test against a full sailing refuses every hold, and the terminal lists them all.

items.title: Expire offline holds after ten minutes
items.summary: A hold made offline lapses after ten minutes, the same as a hold made in the app.

facets.label: Addresses
facets.markdown: Offline holds never expire, and these were six hours old when they replayed.

facets.label: What changes
facets.markdown: The terminal stamps each offline hold with its time, drops it after ten minutes, and tells the clerk which holds lapsed.

facets.label: Note
facets.markdown: The office asked for twenty minutes on busy mornings. Ten matches the app, and a clerk can always hold again.
